Founding Fullstack Engineer TypeScript Web3

Saifuro
$190k - $224k
Remote
 Apply

Saifuro checks payments that AI agents try to make. An agent asks to spend, we compare the request with a mandate a human approved earlier, and the answer comes back signed so the receiving side can verify it. There's escrow on Base and Solana for trades between agents, and settlement is in USDC, onchain. We never hold customer funds. The docs are public at docs.saifuro.com, and the people who use them are developers building agents and the teams selling APIs to those agents.

You'd be one of our first engineers, and you'd lead the product customers log into: the console where a finance team watches its agents spend, the policy editor, the approvals, the sandbox. Founding means you shape what we build as well as how, and you have a say in who joins next. Call it product engineer, full-stack developer or Web3 developer if you prefer.

What you'd be doing

• Foundations. Decide how we build: architecture, testing, deployment and monitoring for the codebase every engineer after you will work in.

• Customers. Talk to the teams integrating Saifuro, see where they get stuck, and ship the fix the same week.

• Onchain. Bring USDC settlement, escrow status and receipts into the product, so every payment can be traced from approval to the chain.

• The product. Build what customers log into, from the database to the screen: what their agents spend, payments waiting for approval, and the record behind every decision.

What we need from you

• You've shipped TypeScript on both sides, a React front end and a Node back end, in a product people paid for.

• You've built against an EVM chain or Solana, with viem, ethers or something like them.

• You live in one of the countries we can hire in.

Beyond these requirements, we'll support you in learning whatever else the role demands. If your experience is relevant but your title differs, we would still like to hear from you. Work outside a job counts too: open source, hackathons and your own projects.

It helps, but isn't required, if you've built dashboards for payments or fintech, if you've worked with Postgres and event streams, if you know Go, if you've built with an agent framework or MCP, or if you've been one of the first engineers somewhere before.

Pay and benefits

• Salary $190,000 to $225,000. That's the US range. Outside the US we pay in USD, or in USDC if you'd rather, and set the offer against the top of the local market.

• Equity: 1.0% of Saifuro, vesting.

• Health: 100% of medical, dental and vision premiums for US employees, 75% for dependents. Outside the US, the local plan through our employer of record, or $300 a month toward private cover.

• 25 days of paid vacation plus your public holidays, and we close between Christmas and New Year.

• 14 weeks of paid parental leave, for any parent.

• A laptop and $1,000 toward your workspace.

• $1,500 a year for learning, conferences included. That's on top of the events you'll attend for work: six to eight a year, planned a quarter ahead, on the company.

Hours are flexible. The one thing we ask is to be online from 14:00 to 17:00 UTC, when the team overlaps for calls and quick questions. That's a window, not the working day. The rest of your hours are yours to arrange. A mainnet incident doesn't keep office hours. If that window is the middle of your night, say so and we'll work something out.

You can combine this with a job at another company, as long as the two don't conflict.

Is Web3 career legit?

▼

As a career, Web3 can be a legitimate and exciting field to work in, as it offers the opportunity to work on cutting-edge technology and help build the infrastructure for a more decentralized and secure internet. Web3 developers and professionals may work on projects related to decentralized finance, non-fungible tokens, decentralized autonomous organizations, and more. While the field is still relatively new and evolving, there is a growing demand for professionals with expertise in Web3, and web3 developer jobs growth are likely to increase in the coming years.

Is it hard to get a job at Web3?

▼

Jobs in crypto can be competitive, as the demand for professionals with expertise in this field has increased in recent years. However, the difficulty of finding a job in the cryptocurrency industry will depend on various factors, such as your qualifications, experience, and the specific job you are seeking. For example, if you have a strong background in computer science, finance, or economics and have relevant experience working in the cryptocurrency industry, you may have an easier time finding a job in this field. On the other hand, if you are new to the industry and do not have any relevant experience or education, it may be more challenging to break into the field. It is also worth noting that the job market in the cryptocurrency industry is constantly evolving, and the specific job opportunities available can vary significantly depending on the current state of the market.

What skills are needed for Web3?

▼

There are a variety of skills that can be beneficial to start your crypto careers in web3 projects. Some of the key skills that may be useful for Web3 professionals include: Programming skills: Web3 professionals should have strong programming skills, particularly in languages such as Solidity (for Ethereum smart contracts) and JavaScript (for building decentralized applications). Blockchain knowledge: Web3 professionals should have a solid understanding of blockchain technology and how it works. Cryptography: Familiarity with cryptographic concepts and techniques, such as hashing and digital signatures, is important for Web3 professionals. Data structures and algorithms: Web3 professionals should have a strong understanding of data structures and algorithms, as they are used extensively in blockchain technology. Networking: Web3 professionals should have a good understanding of networking concepts, as decentralized systems rely on communication between different nodes on a network. Problem-solving skills: Web3 professionals should be able to think creatively and find solutions to complex technical problems. Collaboration skills: Web3 professionals should be able to work well in a team and communicate effectively with colleagues and clients.

How do I get a job with Web3 development?

▼

There are a few steps you can take to increase your chances of finding a job in Web3 development: 1. Build your skills: To work with Web3 technologies, you'll need to have a strong foundation in web development and be proficient in at least one programming language such as JavaScript, Python, or Rust. Consider taking online courses or earning a degree in a related field to gain the necessary skills. 2. Gain experience: Consider working on personal projects or contributing to open-source projects related to Web3 technologies. This will not only help you build your skills, but it will also give you something to showcase in your portfolio and during job interviews. 3. Network: Attend meetups, conferences, and other events related to Web3 technologies to meet people in the industry and learn about job opportunities. You can also reach out to Web3 developers or organizations directly to ask about internships or job openings. 4. Create a strong online presence: Make sure you have a well-written resume and LinkedIn profile that highlight your Web3 skills and experience. Consider creating a portfolio website that showcases your work and accomplishments. 5. Keep learning: The field of Web3 is constantly evolving, so it's important to stay up-to-date on the latest technologies and trends. Consider subscribing to industry publications and participating in online communities to stay current. These steps can significantly improve your chances in crypto career in web3 projects.
